limitations: One run, one optional delivery-dependent task, one supplied effect receipt, and two terminal event subscribers. Terminal request closes admission and captures the first outcome and its available receipt.

Subscriber settlement and delivery are controlled independently. The first rejection remains observable only after the other subscriber settles. The model distinguishes terminal event fanout failure from the original run outcome.

Fair progress assumes the connector, work, event subscribers, and terminal continuation settle when enabled. The model does not prove provider durability, uncooperative callback completion, nested events, or tracker quarantine.

emitResult names the inner fanout result; RunTerminalOwner.request reports rejection through the existing task tracker and resolves. A real runtime case also preserves first-observed error identity and subsequent event-array sequencing; multiple event names are not part of the finite state projection.
